text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: Streaming SLO breach detected for workspace-edge (prod) — p95 > 1.0s, p99 > 10s for /v1/streams/ws (chat/stream) · dashboard: https://redwood/d/streams/alerts
samir: ack. I'm oncall. What's the customer-facing impact? Any 5xx spikes?
pagerduty: Incident triggered and routed to samir (oncall) — priority: P1
leo: seeing the same. Alerts are isolated to websocket streaming endpoints — majority of errors are timeouts/retries, not 500s. SSE less affected.
dina: digging into proxy logs now — seeing long gaps between chunks for a subset of connections. ttfb fine but after initial chunks we get stalled writes.
samir: steps to triage? can we limit blast radius while we investigate?
leo: immediate mitigations to try:
- set nginx proxy_read_timeout and proxy_send_timeout to 60s
- disable proxy_buffering for the stream location
- add a short keepalive ping from edge to client
commands I suggest:
```
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/nginx-proxy -- nginx -s reload
# or patch configmap then
kubectl rollout restart deploy/nginx-proxy
```
dina: proxy logs (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:34Z] upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while sending to client, client: 10.8.4.22, server: edge, request: "GET /v1/streams/ws?session=abc123"
[2026-03-14T09:12:34Z] sent 502, client: 10.8.4.22
```
leo: add config snippet for stream location:
```
location /v1/streams/ws {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_read_timeout 60s;
  proxy_send_timeout 60s;
  sendfile off;
}
```
samir: rolling the proxy config now to test. will watch p95/p99 and number of stalled connections
deploy-bot: Deployment nginx-proxy rollout started by samir — rollout id: r-20260314-1
alex: quick question — which customers are impacted? can we surface by tenant header or IPs?
dina: correlating logs -> ~4 tenants show elevated retry rates. sample metrics: p95=1.32s, p99=12.4s, error_rate_streams=3.8% (baseline 0.2%).
```
metric:streams.p95 1.32
metric:streams.p99 12.4
metric:streams.errors.percent 3.8
```
samir: root cause hypotheses: client-side slow consumers causing backpressure; nginx upstream buffers filling; kernel send buffers hitting limits; or a change in browser behaviour causing slower reads.
leo: leaning toward proxy buffering + slow client reads. chrome 116 had similar regressions previously where WS read scheduling changed. short-term: reduce proxy_buffers and worker_conn increase; medium-term: move heavy tenants to dedicated streaming pool and instrument per-connection stall metrics.
dina: netstat on edge shows many ESTABLISHED with small send-q:
```
tcp 0 12345 10.8.4.22:443 ESTABLISHED 0 0
tcp 0 0 10.8.4.33:443 ESTABLISHED 1024 0
```
samir: action list (short-term):
- rolled nginx proxy config to disable buffering and bump timeouts (samir) :white_check_mark:
- enabled keepalive ping in edge (leo) :white_check_mark:
- increased worker_connections to 65536 (leo) :white_check_mark:
- started telemetry collection for per-connection stall (dina) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
- identify top 5 tenants with repeated stalls and route to dedicated pool (follow-up)
maria: I'm taking the morning oncall handoff — please add a brief doc with what we changed and links to dashboards + logs. Also open a post-incident doc if we land on config root cause.
samir: handing off. summary: we mitigated immediate connection stalls by disabling proxy_buffering and increasing timeouts; ongoing work: telemetry, tenant routing, kernel tuning, and customer outreach. Handoff to maria at 2026-03-14T10:30Z.
oncall-bot: Handoff created -> incident #INC-20260314-21 assigned to maria. Handoff notes: https://redwood/incidents/INC-20260314-21
maria: acknowledged — will pick up and loop in PM/support to notify affected tenants. :thumbsup:
